name: laya
description: Laya is an Apache-2.0 multilingual non-autoregressive decision model that answers typed questions (choices, scores, booleans) over text or JSON states with calibrated probabilities in a single ~33 ms forward pass, auto-routing across three checkpoints covering 100+ languages.

name: cua-s1-forms
description: cua-s1-forms is a 706K-parameter single-pass option scorer that maps a GUI form element plus typed candidates (fill each extracted entity, check, click, skip) to per-option probabilities, letting cua-driver fill and submit forms without an autoregressive LLM.

name: sales-conversion-model-reinf-learning
description: A Stable Baselines3 PPO reinforcement-learning model that predicts sales conversion probability turn-by-turn (96.7% accuracy, 85ms inference) from conversation embeddings and LLM-derived engagement/effectiveness metrics, enabling real-time sales coaching and quantitative A/B testing of scripts.

name: Arch-Router-1.5B
description: Arch-Router-1.5B is a compact Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct-based text-generation model that maps conversation intent to user-defined domain/action routes and outputs JSON route selections, enabling transparent, configurable, low-latency routing to preferred LLMs.

name: laya-grounded
description: A fine-tune of the laya typed-decision model that improves grounding on explicitly stated facts, consistency between logical inverses, and probability calibration, at the cost of worse phishing detection and option-name routing stability.

name: laya-vision-smolvlm-256m
description: A SmolVLM-256M-based vision-language decision model that produces calibrated multiple-choice and yes/no probabilities for an image plus optional text in one non-generative forward pass, enabling fast confidence-aware visual question answering (~71 ms on an NVIDIA L4).

name: gliclass-modern-base-v2.0-init
description: A 151M-parameter ModernBERT-based GLiClass model that performs efficient zero-shot multi-label text labeling in a single forward pass, supporting topic tagging, sentiment analysis, NLI-style premise–hypothesis scoring, and RAG reranking with cross-encoder-level accuracy at lower compute.
